o1.biggest_strength: It leads with the real buying and return drivers: 5 to 12 cards, about 10 flat notes, 10/14 mm thickness, small coin pouch, and first-week snugness.
o1.biggest_mistake: It adds an internal measurement section and assumptions to a customer-facing deliverable, and the add-to-cart line misses the useful break-in reassurance.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Remove the internal testing notes, keep the page under the requested limit, and use the under-button line to say the card slots are snug for the first week.

o2.biggest_strength: It handles the main objections plainly above the fold, especially cash capacity, card break-in and who should choose a larger wallet.
o2.biggest_mistake: It invents or implies extra capacity in places, especially that the hidden pocket takes one more flat note and that 12 cards plus 10 notes is still about 14 mm thick.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Remove the unverified hidden-pocket cash claim, avoid implying max-card-plus-max-cash thickness, and tighten the SEO title to around 60 characters.

reason: Output 1 is the safer page to publish because it is more precise about capacity and less likely to create the exact cash-expectation returns we are trying to cut. Output 2 is strong, but its small overclaims are on the highest-risk part of the page.
